the prevalence of FMS mastery is significantly lower in overweight/obese compared with non‐obese children.

The main takeaway from our work is that
children who are overweight or obese are at a higher risk of developing poor motor proficiency, and that motor proficiency is not a given for children.
overweight and obese children are less likely to master fundamental movement skills compared with their peers of the same age and sex.
